'''Jerome J. Workman Jr.''' is an American analytical spectroscopist, author, editor, and inventor born on August 6, 1952,&nbsp;in Northfield,&nbsp;Minnesota. '''Jerry Workman''', '''Jerry Workman, Jr.''', and '''J.J. Workman''' are also names he uses for publishing.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ca.pittcon.org/technical+program/TPAbstra09.nsf/SA/FC09E291EFB28C41852574860051B307?opendocument |title=Session: Williams-Wright Award |publisher=Ca.pittcon.org |date=2009-03-11 |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/-/e/B001HD0SR4 |title=Jerry Workman: Books, Biography, Blog, Audiobooks, Kindle |website=Amazon |date= |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref><ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|url=http://www.astm.org/SNEWS/OCTOBER_2002/workman_oct02.html |title=SN E13 Feature |publisher=Astm.org |date= |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spectroscopynow.com/coi/cda/detail.cda?id=1881&type=EducationFeature&chId=2&page=1#Refs |title=Home |publisher=spectroscopyNOW.com |date= |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.labbusinessmag.com/archives/2009/LB_Summer09.pdf |title=Lab Business : Summer 2009 |publisher=Labbusinessmag.com |access-date=2013-10-22 |archive-date=2013-10-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019090522/http://www.labbusinessmag.com/archives/2009/LB_Summer09.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Workman was born on August 06, 1952, in Northfield, Minnesota. He attended [[Saint John's University (Minnesota)]] and later completed a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] (''[[Latin honors|cum laude]])'' degree, followed by a [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] from [[Saint Mary's University of Minnesota]]. While at St. John's, Workman was co-captain of the wrestling team, two times Minnesota Intercollegiate Athletic Conference (MIAC) Champion (1971,1974) and later became head wrestling coach at St. Mary's in 1976.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.miacathletics.com/about/honor_history/records/wrest |title=MIAC Wrestling Recordbook |publisher=MIAC |access-date=2021-07-09 |archive-date=2014-03-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140318061336/http://www.miacathletics.com/about/honor_history/records/wrest |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gojohnnies.com/sports/2008/7/21/WRESTLING_MIAC%20Champions.aspx?id=34 |title= SJU Wrestling MIAC Champions (1948–2004) |publisher=SJU |access-date=2021-07-09 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://issuu.com/smumn/docs/smm_s16 |title=Saint Mary's Magazine |date=30 March 2016 |publisher=SMU, p. 56. |access-date=2021-07-09 }}</ref> In addition, he was a National Catholic Intercollegiate Tournament (NCIT) Champion and was voted Outstanding Wrestler of the NCIT Tournament  in 1972.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://cdm.csbsju.edu/digital/collection/SJUArchives/id/6920 |title= 1971-72-12 SJU Alumni Magazine Volume 11 Number 03 Winter |publisher=SJU |access-date=2021-07-09 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.csbsju.edu/sju-archives/sjuhistory/booksaboutstjohns/scoreboardbook/scoreboardchapter8 |title=SJU Archives |publisher=SJU |access-date=2021-07-09 }}</ref>

He went on to earn his PhD at [[Columbia Pacific University]].{{citation needed |date=December 2021}} Later, he entered the Columbia Executive Program at the [[Columbia Business School]], completing the [[Columbia Senior Executive Program]], the [[Certificate in Business Excellence]], and the Certificate of Executive Development. At [[MIT Sloan School of Management]] he did further studies for a Certificate in Strategy and Innovation.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zale |first=Liz |url=http://www.columbia.edu/cu/news/05/03/jerryWorkman.html |title=Columbia News ::: Business School Executive Education Program Grooms Leaders |publisher=Columbia.edu |date= |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.columbia.edu/cu/record/archives/vol30/vol30_iss9/page12.pdf |title=Saffron-Colored Spectacles |publisher=Columbia.edu |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://executive.mit.edu/executivecertificates/community/ |title=Certificate Holders – Executive Network – MIT Sloan Executive Education |publisher=Executive.mit.edu |date= |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref>

==Career==
Workman has held appointments with the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|U.S. National Academies]] [[United States National Research Council|NRC]] panel for Assessment of [[NIST]] Programs from 2005 to 2007 and was given the [[U.S. Department of Commerce]] Certificate of Appreciation in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nist.gov/director/nrc/upload/CSTLFinalCameraReady.pdf |title=An Assessment of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Chemical Science and Technology Laboratory : Fiscal Year 2007 |publisher=Nist.gov |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref> He has served as executive editor (editor-in-chief) of ''[[List of scientific journals in chemistry|Spectroscopy Letters]]'', appointed 1999–2003; associate editor, ''[[Applied Spectroscopy Reviews]]'' (New York), appointed 1999–2004; editorial advisory board, and ''[[Spectroscopy Magazine]]'' (Oregon) since 1995.{{citation needed |date=December 2021}} He was a Charter Member of [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]] PAT and Chemometrics Committee in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fda.gov/ohrms/dockets/ac/02/transcripts/3869T2.doc |access-date=July 2, 2010 |url-status=dead |title=FDA Dockets 2002|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100309104540/https://www.fda.gov/ohrms/dockets/ac/02/transcripts/3869T2.doc |archive-date=March 9, 2010 |website=[[Food and Drug Administration]] }}</ref> Workman has also been a member of various chemical and scientific advisory boards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.astm.org/SNEWS/APRIL_2001/index.html |title=Standardization News Home Page |publisher=Astm.org |date= |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1021/ac070765q |pmid=17474712 |title=Process Analytical Chemistry  |journal=Analytical Chemistry |volume=79 |issue=12 |pages=4345–63 |date=2007-06-15 |last1=Workman |first1=Jerome |last2=Koch |first2=Mel |last3=Veltkamp |first3=Dave }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://depts.washington.edu/cpac/Research/nonproprietary.html |title=CPAC – Nonproprietary Manuscripts |publisher=Depts.washington.edu |date= |access-date=2013-10-22}}</ref> Workman is also the holder of multiple patents, including twenty issued US patents.<ref name="Patpf.uspto.gov">{{cite web|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-bool.html&r=0&f=S&l=50&TERM1=Workman&FIELD1=INNM&co1=AND&TERM2=Jerome&FIELD2=INNM&d=PTXT |title=US Patent & Trademark Office, Patent Full Text and Image Database |publisher=Patpf.uspto.gov |access-date=2013-10-23}}</ref><ref name="Appft.uspto.gov">{{cite web|url=http://appft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-bool.html&r=0&f=S&l=50&TERM1=Workman&FIELD1=IN&co1=AND&TERM2=Jerome&FIELD2=IN&d=PG01 |title=US Patent & Trademark Office, Patent Full Text and Image Database |publisher=Appft.uspto.gov |access-date=2013-10-23}}</ref>

In 1997 Workman worked with Elsevier Author Services as an editor of chief. Workman authored the three-volume ''Academic Press Handbook of Organic Compounds'', and five-volume ''The Concise Handbook of Analytical Spectroscopy''.<ref name="The Academic Press Handbook of Organic Compounds">{{cite book |last1=Workman |first1=Jerome |url=https://www.elsevier.com/books/the-handbook-of-organic-compounds-three-volume-set/workman-jr/978-0-12-763560-6 |title=The Academic Press Handbook of Organic Compounds: NIR, IR, Raman, and UV-VIS Spectra Featuring Polymers, and Surfactants, (3 Volume Set: Vol. 1, Methods and Interpretation; Vol. 2, UV-Vis and NIR Spectra; Vol. 3, IR and Raman Spectra) |date=2000 |publisher=Academic Press, Boston |isbn=978-0127635606 |access-date=23 December 2021}}</ref><ref name="The Concise Handbook of Analytical Spectroscopy">{{cite book |last1=Workman |first1=Jerome |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/8800 |title=The Concise Handbook of Analytical Spectroscopy: Physical Foundations, Techniques, Instrumentation and Data Analysis, In 5 Volumes, UV, Vis, NIR, IR, and Raman |date=2016 |publisher=Imperial College Press |isbn=9789814508056 |volume=1 |doi=10.1142/8800 |access-date=23 December 2021}}</ref> He, along with co-author Howard L. Mark, have published over 150 successive columns on statistics and [[chemometrics]] for ''[[Spectroscopy Magazine]]'' since 1986.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chemometrics in Spectroscopy Column |url=http://spectroscopyonline.findanalytichem.com/Chemometrics+in+Spectroscopy+Column |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100527144132/http://spectroscopyonline.findanalytichem.com/Chemometrics%2Bin%2BSpectroscopy%2BColumn |archive-date=May 27, 2010 |access-date=July 2, 2010}}</ref> He has received the [[Williams–Wright Award]], the [[ASTM International Award of Merit]],<ref>{{cite web |title=ASTM International Award Membership |url=http://www.astm.org/MEMBERSHIP/Docs/E13.doc |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110617012730/http://www.astm.org/MEMBERSHIP/Docs/E13.doc |archive-date=June 17, 2011 |access-date=July 2, 2010}}</ref> the [[Eastern Analytical Symposium|Eastern Analytical Symposium Award]],<ref>{{Cite journal |author=Jce Staff |date=2009-08-03 |title=News and Announcements |journal=Journal of Chemical Education |volume=79 |issue=5 |pages=555 |doi=10.1021/ed079p555 |doi-access=free}}</ref> and the [[Society for Applied Spectroscopy|New York Society for Applied Spectroscopy Gold Medal Award]] for his considerable volume of publications, reviews, and books.<ref>{{cite web |date=10 February 2020 |title=Workman and Mark Win Gold Medal Award from the New York Society for Applied Spectroscopy |url=https://www.spectroscopyonline.com/view/workman-and-mark-win-gold-medal-award-new-york-society-applied-spectroscopy |access-date=February 24, 2021}}</ref>
